text: Git branching is an essential part of version control, helping developers work on new features without disrupting the main code. A feature branch is created from the main branch, allowing changes to be tested safely. Once the work is complete, the branch is merged back into the main codebase. In team settings, developers often use pull requests before merging. A pull request is a request to review and approve the changes, which encourages collaboration and reduces errors. This workflow keeps the project organized, ensures code quality, and makes it easy to track what was changed and why. Overall, Git branching provides a clear and efficient way to manage software development.
